sets.title: Learning to sail at fifty-two
sets.intro: Six sentences have been removed from the article. Choose from the sentences A-G the one which fits each gap. There is one extra sentence you do not need to use.
text: At the age of fifty-two, Daniel Osei decided to learn something he had always found intimidating: sailing. {{1}} He signed up for a short beginner's course at a sailing club on the coast.
The first lesson did not go smoothly. {{2}} Still, the instructor reassured him that almost everyone capsizes at least once during their first few sessions.
By the third week, something had changed. {{3}} Daniel found himself looking forward to each session rather than dreading it.
He also noticed changes beyond the water. {{4}} His colleagues began to comment that he seemed calmer under pressure at work.

Not everything about the hobby was easy to explain to friends. {{5}} Daniel simply tells people that sailing forces him to concentrate on one thing at a time, which he rarely manages to do anywhere else.

Eighteen months later, Daniel has passed two further qualifications and is considering buying a small boat of his own. {{6}} For him, the biggest surprise was not learning to sail itself, but discovering how much he had needed a hobby that asked for his full attention.

options.text: He capsized twice within the first hour and swallowed what felt like half the sea.
His wife had given him a sailing lesson voucher as a joke birthday present, never expecting him to actually use it.
He began reading about sailing late at night and found himself calculating wind directions during his daily commute.
He started arriving at meetings early instead of rushing in at the last minute, something that was entirely new for him.
Explaining why getting shouted at by the wind and nearly falling into cold water counts as relaxing is not straightforward.
He now plans to spend most weekends on the water once the better weather arrives.
Several of his friends had already taken up similar outdoor hobbies after retiring early.

questions.explanation: B explains how Daniel came to try sailing at all, which leads naturally into 'He signed up for a short beginner's course'.
A gives a concrete example of the lesson 'not going smoothly', and repeats 'capsize', which the next sentence also uses.
C shows the change in Daniel's attitude ('something had changed') that leads into him looking forward to sessions.
D describes a change 'beyond the water' (at work), which is exactly what the colleagues then comment on.
E gives the specific difficulty of explaining the hobby, which 'Daniel simply tells people...' then resolves.
F describes his plans for the sport, fitting naturally before the concluding sentence about his biggest surprise.

extra.explanation: The text is about Daniel's personal experience; his friends' own hobbies are never otherwise mentioned, so G fits nowhere.
